01 The QA operating model3 p

QA at Lingotran is not a phase at the end of a sprint. It is a set of gates, each with an owner and an exit condition. If you cannot name the gate a piece of work is sitting at, you cannot say whether it is ready.

1.1 What QA owns, and what it does not

ActivityOwnerQA's actual job
Unit testsDeveloperRead them in the PR. Judge whether they assert behaviour or implementation. Do not write them.
Acceptance criteriaQA + POWritten as Given/When/Then before the sprint opens. QA drafts, PO confirms.
Integration testsDeveloper + QAQA specifies the cases; either party implements.
End-to-end suiteQAOwned outright — authorship, stability, runtime, and the decision to delete flaky specs.
Exploratory chartersQATime-boxed, documented, and the single highest-yield activity in this table.
Performance baselinesQA + SREQA owns the scenario; SRE owns the infrastructure it runs against.
Release go/no-goQAQA states risk in plain language. The business decides. QA never says "it's fine".
Production monitoringSREQA defines what "wrong" looks like so alerts can be written against it.

1.2 Quality gates

GateExit conditionBlocks what
ReadyACs testable, edge cases named, test data identifiedStory entering the sprint
PRBuild green, coverage on changed lines ≥ 80%, QA comment resolvedMerge to main
IntegrationAPI suite green against a real PostgreSQL containerDeploy to staging
StagingE2E green, exploratory charter complete, a11y scan cleanRelease candidate
ReleaseReadiness report signed, rollback rehearsedProduction deploy
Post-deploySmoke green on production, error rate flat for 30 minClosing the release
Coverage gates are gamed

A global "80% coverage" target is met by testing getters. Gate on coverage of changed lines in the diff instead. It is the only coverage number that resists gaming, because it moves only when the author writes tests for the code they just wrote.

1.3 Risk-based prioritisation

Everything cannot be tested. Score each area, test in descending order, and be able to defend the order out loud.

Lingotran areaImpactLikelihoodScoreWhy
Login & session5420Total lockout for a whole school; changes often
Speech capture & scoring5420The product's reason to exist; browser and device variance is huge
Lesson progress persistence5315Lost progress destroys trust and is unrecoverable
Teacher class reports4312Drives renewal conversations with institutions
Role-based access5210A student seeing another class's data is a safeguarding incident
Billing & seat counts428Contractual exposure, but changes rarely
Marketing pages133Embarrassing, not damaging
The institution multiplier

Lingotran sells to schools, not individuals. Every defect is multiplied by class size before anyone notices it. A bug affecting one learner is a ticket; the same bug on a shared classroom network is thirty simultaneous tickets and an escalation to the head of department. Weight likelihood accordingly.

2.2 The layer trace — what QA validates at each hop

This is the core device of the manual. Any Lingotran request passes through these layers. When a PR changes one, you test that row and re-test every row below it.

1
React componentLessonPlayer.tsx
Loading, empty, error and success states all render. Disabled controls during submit. No secrets in props. Keyboard reachable.
2
API clientlib/apiClient.ts
Correlation ID attached. Timeout set. 401 triggers refresh exactly once, not a loop. Network failure surfaces a retry, not a blank screen.
3
Routeroutes/*.routes.ts
HTTP verb and path correct. Auth middleware present — and present on every sibling route, which is where it is usually missing.
4
Middlewareauthenticate, rateLimit
Order matters: validate before authenticate leaks schema; authenticate before rateLimit lets unauthenticated floods through. Check the order, not just the presence.
5
Validatorzod schema
Unknown keys stripped. Type coercion explicit. Error shape identical across endpoints. Rejects before any DB call.
6
Controller*.controller.ts
Maps result to status code. No business logic. No SQL. Never leaks an internal error message to the client.
7
Service*.service.ts
Where the rules live, so where most bugs live. Ownership checks, quota checks, state transitions. Test this layer hardest.
8
Repository*.repository.ts
Parameterised queries only. Transaction boundary wraps multi-write operations. Soft-delete filter applied.
9
PostgreSQLschema + indexes
Constraint enforces what code assumes. Index supports the query's WHERE. Migration is reversible.
10
ResponseJSON envelope
Shape matches the contract. Status code semantically right. No internal IDs, stack traces, or row counts.
11
React renderstate update
Optimistic update rolls back on failure. Stale response from a superseded request is discarded, not rendered.
Use it as a diff checklist

Open the PR, mark which layers the diff touches, and test that layer plus everything downstream. A change at layer 7 cannot break layer 1, but a change at layer 9 can break all ten above it.

2.3 Environments

EnvDataSpeech backendWhat it can and cannot prove
LocalSeed script, ~200 rowsStubbed JSONLogic only. Proves nothing about latency, scale, or real audio.
CIEphemeral container per runStubbedRegression and contract. Deterministic by design.
StagingAnonymised copy, ~2M rowsReal, separate quotaThe only place index and query-plan problems appear before production.
ProductionLiveRealRead-only smoke against a dedicated canary account. Never exploratory testing.
The 200-row lie

PostgreSQL will happily seq-scan 200 rows faster than it uses an index, so a missing index is invisible locally and in CI. It appears as gradually rising latency in production, then a timeout cliff. Any query added in a PR must be checked with EXPLAIN against staging volumes, not local.

2.4 Configuration and multi-instance behaviour

Lingotran's API runs on two or more App Service instances. Anything holding state in process memory behaves differently in production than on your laptop.

In-process stateProduction consequenceTest approach
Rate limiter countersEffective limit = configured × instance countRun staging at 2 instances and count actual rejections
In-memory cacheStale reads depending on which instance served youRepeat the same read 10× and compare
Scheduled job timersJob fires once per instance — duplicate emailsAssert exactly-one side effect, not "at least one"
WebSocket session mapReconnect lands on the other instance and loses contextForce a reconnect mid-lesson

2.5 Feature flags

FlagDefaultQA obligation
phoneme_scoring_v2OffTest both states. Off is what most schools run; on is what the demo shows.
keep_signed_inOffTest the transition — a session created while off, then read while on.
offline_lesson_cacheOffFlag flipped mid-session must not corrupt stored progress.
Rule

A flag doubles the state space of everything it touches. Test the transition, not just the two states — flags are flipped on live systems with users mid-lesson.

03 Requirements to test design4 p

3.1 Interrogating a story

Story LT-1187 · Sprint 42

As a teacher using Lingotran on my classroom laptop, I want a "Keep me signed in" option, so I don't re-authenticate between lessons.

AC1 Checkbox appears, unchecked by default. AC2 Checked → session persists 30 days; unchecked → 12 hours. AC3 The choice is not remembered between visits.

A junior engineer writes three test cases, one per criterion. Shashi Kumar writes none yet, and asks seven questions first:

Question the ACs do not answerWhy it changes the test plan
30 days from login, or 30 days of sliding inactivity?Different implementations and different security postures
What happens to an existing 12-hour session if the user logs in again with the box checked?Session upgrade is undefined; both behaviours are defensible
Does a password change invalidate 30-day sessions?If not, a compromised account stays compromised after the "fix"
Is this offered to student accounts on shared classroom devices?A 30-day session on a shared laptop is a safeguarding issue, not a UX preference
Can an admin see and revoke long-lived sessions?Without revocation the feature has no off switch during an incident
What does /refresh do with a 30-day token?Refresh chaining can extend a session indefinitely, defeating both limits
Is 30 days compatible with signed district contracts?Some education contracts cap session lifetime explicitly
The economics

Every question above came from reading three lines against an architecture diagram and a customer profile — before any code existed. Answering them costs one refinement conversation. Finding them in production costs an incident, a rollback, and possibly a contract.

3.2 Rewriting ACs as executable criteria

# Given/When/Then agreed before the sprint opens — this becomes the Playwright spec
Scenario: Teacher opts into an extended session
  Given a teacher account at a school with extended sessions permitted
  When they sign in with "Keep me signed in" checked
  Then the refresh token expires in 30 days
   And the session appears in Admin › Active sessions as revocable

Scenario: Student accounts are excluded
  Given a student account
  When they open the sign-in form
  Then the "Keep me signed in" control is not rendered

Scenario: Password change ends all extended sessions
  Given a teacher with an active 30-day session on a second device
  When they change their password
  Then the second device receives 401 on its next request

3.3 Technique reference

TechniqueUse whenLingotran example
Equivalence partitioningInput space is too large to enumerateRecording length: <1s (reject), 1–60s (accept), >60s (reject) — three cases, not three hundred
Boundary valuesAny range, always0.9s, 1.0s, 1.1s, 59.9s, 60.0s, 60.1s — bugs cluster at the edge, never the middle
Decision tableMultiple conditions combinerole × flag × network → whether the control renders
State transitionAn entity has a lifecycleLesson: not-started → in-progress → submitted → scored → returned
PairwiseCombinatorial explosion4 browsers × 3 OS × 3 mic types = 36; pairwise covers the interactions in 9
Error guessingYou have read the codeUnbounded loops, missing await, unfiltered soft-deletes

3.4 Boundary analysis worked — audio submission

ParameterRuleValues to testExpected
Clip duration1–60 s0.99 / 1.00 / 1.01 / 59.99 / 60.00 / 60.01422 / 200 / 200 / 200 / 200 / 422
File size≤ 5 MB5 242 879 / 5 242 880 / 5 242 881 bytes200 / 200 / 413
Attempts per exercise≤ 33rd attempt / 4th attempt200 / 429 with retry hint
Display name1–80 chars0 / 1 / 80 / 81 chars; 80 emoji; 80 Devanagari422 / 200 / 200 / 422 / 200 / 200
Class size≤ 200 seats200th enrol / 201st enrol200 / 409 seat limit
Length is not character count

An 80-character limit enforced with str.length in JavaScript counts UTF-16 code units. "🎓" is 2, and a Devanagari cluster can be 4+. A learner named in Hindi or Tamil hits an 80-character limit at 20 visible characters. Always test the limit with non-Latin script — this is Lingotran's core user base.

04 Frontend testing · React4 p

4.1 Reading a component as QA

src/features/lesson/RecordControl.tsx
export function RecordControl({ exerciseId, maxAttempts = 3 }: Props) {
  const [state, setState] = useState<'idle'|'recording'|'uploading'|'scored'|'error'>('idle');
  const [attempts, setAttempts] = useState(0);              // ① client-side counter
  const recorder = useRef<MediaRecorder|null>(null);

  async function start() {
    const stream = await navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia({ audio: true }); // ② can reject
    recorder.current = new MediaRecorder(stream, { mimeType: 'audio/webm' });   // ③ Safari
    setState('recording');
  }

  async function stop() {
    setState('uploading');
    const blob = await collect(recorder.current!);
    try {
      const r = await api.post(`/exercises/${exerciseId}/attempts`, blob);
      setAttempts(a => a + 1);                                 // ④ only on success
      setState('scored');
    } catch { setState('error'); }                           // ⑤ no retry offered
  }
  ...
}
#What QA reads hereTest that falls out of it
①Attempt count lives in component stateReload the page mid-exercise — does the limit reset? Server must be the authority.
②getUserMedia can reject: denied, dismissed, no device, device in useFour distinct denial paths, each needing its own message. Deny once, then re-open — most apps never recover.
③Hard-coded audio/webmSafari and iPad Safari do not produce webm. Test on real iPad — the school's actual device.
④Counter increments only on successFail the upload 5× — user gets unlimited attempts. Network throttle to trigger.
⑤catch sets error, offers nothingDead end for the learner. A classroom of 30 hitting this generates 30 support tickets.

4.2 States every Lingotran view must handle

StateHow to force itCommon defect
LoadingDevTools throttle to Slow 3GLayout shift when content arrives; no skeleton
EmptyFresh account, no lessonsBlank panel instead of a next action
ErrorBlock the endpoint in DevToolsInfinite spinner; raw error text shown
PartialLesson loads, scores endpoint failsWhole page fails when one panel could degrade
StaleTwo tabs, edit in oneSecond tab overwrites with old data
OfflineDevTools offline mid-lessonProgress silently lost — the highest-severity frontend class
Slow responseDelay 8 sDouble submit; two attempts recorded

4.3 Race conditions

// Learner switches lesson quickly. Response for lesson A arrives after lesson B's.
useEffect(() => {
  let cancelled = false;                       // ← the guard QA looks for
  api.get(`/lessons/${id}`).then(r => {
    if (!cancelled) setLesson(r.data);
  });
  return () => { cancelled = true; };
}, [id]);
If that guard is absent

Click lesson A then lesson B fast on a throttled connection: the screen shows lesson B's title with lesson A's content. Learners submit answers to the wrong exercise. Reproduce with Slow 3G and two rapid clicks — impossible to hit on a fast laptop, trivial on school wifi.

IDCaseExpectedLayer

LT-F02Record on iPad SafariClip captured and uploadedManual, real device
LT-F03Upload fails 3× consecutivelyAttempt counter unchanged; retry offeredComponent

LT-F05Rapid lesson switch on Slow 3GContent always matches titleE2E

05 API testing · Node & Express4 p

5.1 Middleware order is a test case

src/routes/attempt.routes.ts
router.post('/exercises/:id/attempts',
  rateLimit({ windowMs: 60_000, max: 10 }),   // ① in-process — see 2.4
  authenticate,                                // ② JWT verify
  authorize('learner'),                        // ③ role
  validate(attemptSchema),                     // ④ body shape
  attemptController.create
);

router.get('/exercises/:id/attempts', authenticate, attemptController.list);
router.delete('/attempts/:id', attemptController.remove);   // ⑤ no auth — audit siblings
#Test
①Two instances → real limit is 20/min, not 10. Verify against staging at production instance count.
②Expired, malformed, alg:none, valid token signed with the wrong key, token for a deleted user.
③Teacher token on a learner route → 403 not 500. Learner token on a teacher route → 403.
④Unknown fields stripped, not stored. Extra {"role":"admin"} in the body must not escalate.
⑤Always audit sibling routes. One unguarded verb on a resource undoes the guards on the others.

5.2 Contract

POST /api/v1/exercises/8821/attempts        Authorization: Bearer <jwt>
                                            X-Correlation-Id: 8f2c1a94-...
{ "clipUrl": "https://blob.../a12.webm", "durationMs": 4820 }

201 { "attemptId":"at_9931", "score":{"accuracy":82,"fluency":76},
      "attemptsRemaining":2 }
422 { "error":{"code":"CLIP_TOO_SHORT","message":"Recording must be at least 1 second",
                "field":"durationMs"} }
429 { "error":{"code":"ATTEMPT_LIMIT","retryAfter":3600} }
StatusConditionTest
201Valid clip within limitsBody matches schema exactly; no extra fields leaked
400Malformed JSONSame envelope shape as every other 4xx
401Missing/expired tokenMessage identical for both — no oracle for attackers
403Exercise belongs to another class403 not 404 — but confirm which the team chose, and be consistent
404Exercise does not existMust not differ in timing from 403 (see 9.2)
409Attempt already in flightIdempotency under double submit
413Clip > 5 MBRejected at the gateway, before the app
422Duration out of rangeField name present so UI can highlight it
429Attempt or rate limitretryAfter present and honest
502Azure AI Speech unavailableClip retained; learner told to retry; attempt not consumed

5.3 Service layer — where the rules are

src/services/attempt.service.ts
async function create(userId: string, exerciseId: string, clip: Clip) {
  const ex = await repo.findExercise(exerciseId);
  if (!ex) throw new NotFound();
  if (!await repo.userInClass(userId, ex.classId)) throw new Forbidden();  // ① ownership

  const used = await repo.countAttempts(userId, exerciseId);
  if (used >= ex.maxAttempts) throw new TooMany();                        // ② check…

  const score = await speech.assess(clip, ex.referenceText);              // ③ external
  return repo.insertAttempt({ userId, exerciseId, score });                // ④ …then write
}
Check-then-act is a race

Steps ② and ④ are not atomic. Two concurrent submissions both read used = 2, both pass, both insert — a 4th attempt exists on a 3-attempt exercise. Only a unique constraint or a transaction with row locking fixes it. Test: fire two identical requests simultaneously and assert exactly one succeeds. Sequential testing can never find this.

③ costs money and can fail

Assert that a Speech failure does not consume an attempt, does not leave an orphan row, and does not lose the learner's clip.

06 Database testing · PostgreSQL4 p

6.1 Schema QA must know

CREATE TABLE users (
  id            uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  email         citext NOT NULL UNIQUE,        -- case-insensitive by type
  role          text NOT NULL CHECK (role IN ('learner','teacher','admin')),
  school_id     uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES schools(id),
  deleted_at    timestamptz                    -- soft delete: every query must filter
);

CREATE TABLE attempts (
  id            uuid PRIMARY KEY,
  user_id       uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  exercise_id   uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES exercises(id),
  accuracy      numeric(5,2) CHECK (accuracy BETWEEN 0 AND 100),
  created_at    timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
CREATE INDEX idx_attempts_user_ex ON attempts(user_id, exercise_id);
ElementTest that proves it works
citext emailInsert A@school.edu, then a@school.edu — second must be rejected, else two accounts share a login
CHECK on roleDirect SQL insert of role='superadmin' must fail — proves the DB, not just the app, enforces it
ON DELETE CASCADEDelete a user, confirm attempts vanish. Then ask whether that is legal under the school's data-retention contract
deleted_atSoft-delete a learner, then run every list endpoint — one will still return them
Composite indexEXPLAIN the attempt-count query on staging; must be Index Scan, not Seq Scan
numeric(5,2)Score of 99.999 → rounds or errors? Confirm which, and that the UI agrees

6.2 SQL validation queries

-- Orphans: attempts whose exercise was hard-deleted
SELECT a.id FROM attempts a LEFT JOIN exercises e ON e.id = a.exercise_id
WHERE e.id IS NULL;

-- Soft-deleted users still reachable through a join
SELECT u.email FROM users u JOIN attempts a ON a.user_id = u.id
WHERE u.deleted_at IS NOT NULL;

-- Attempt-limit violations that the check-then-act race allowed through
SELECT user_id, exercise_id, count(*) FROM attempts
GROUP BY 1,2 HAVING count(*) > 3;

-- Cross-school leakage: a learner with attempts on another school's exercise
SELECT u.id FROM attempts a
  JOIN users u ON u.id = a.user_id
  JOIN exercises e ON e.id = a.exercise_id
WHERE u.school_id <> e.school_id;                -- must return zero rows, always

-- Is the query actually using the index?
EXPLAIN ANALYZE SELECT count(*) FROM attempts
WHERE user_id = $1 AND exercise_id = $2;
The cross-school query is the single most valuable check in this manual

Run it after any change to enrolment, class assignment, or reporting. A non-zero result means one school can see another school's learner data. That is a contract-terminating event, and it is invisible from the UI.

6.3 Migrations

Migration typeRiskQA action
Add nullable columnLowConfirm old API version still works — deploys are not atomic
Add NOT NULL columnHighRequires a default or a backfill; locks the table without one
Add indexMediumMust be CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY, or writes block during deploy
Rename columnHighBreaks the running old version mid-deploy. Expand/contract over two releases.
Drop columnHighIrreversible. Confirm no code path and no report reads it.
Change typeHighFull table rewrite plus lock. Test on a staging-sized copy and time it.
Rollback is a test case, not a hope

Every migration must be run down in staging before the release is approved. A migration without a tested rollback turns a 10-minute incident into a 4-hour one. Assert that data written after the up-migration survives the down-migration.

07 The speech pipeline3 p

This is the module that matters most, because it is the only part of Lingotran a competitor cannot copy from a screenshot — and the only part where "the tests pass" and "the product works" routinely disagree.

7.1 The path

Mic ──▶ getUserMedia ──▶ MediaRecorder ──▶ Blob ──▶ POST /attempts
                                                        │
                              ┌─────────────────────────┘
                              ▼
                   Azure AI Speech · Pronunciation Assessment
                   (reference text + audio → accuracy, fluency,
                    completeness, per-phoneme scores)
                              │
                              ▼
              Service maps raw scores → learner-facing feedback
                              │
                              ▼
                        attempts table ──▶ progress report ──▶ teacher dashboard

7.2 Why this pipeline is unusually hard to test

PropertyConsequence for QA
Non-deterministicThe same clip can score 81 then 83. Assertions must use tolerance bands, never equality.
External and paidCI cannot call it on every run. Stub in CI; use a small real-audio suite nightly.
Device-dependentA laptop mic, an iPad mic, and a classroom headset produce materially different scores from the same speaker.
Accent-sensitiveThe failure mode is systematic, not random — see 7.4. This is the defect class most likely to reach production unnoticed.
Silently degradingIf the service returns a default or partial payload, the app shows a plausible score. Nothing looks broken.

7.3 The reference clip corpus

Maintain a fixed set of recordings in blob storage. Every release is scored against them and compared to the previous release. This is the only reliable regression signal for scoring quality.

ClipContentExpected bandCatches
REF-01Native speaker, clean audio, correct90–100Baseline drift
REF-02Learner, accented, correct words70–90Accent penalty — the critical one
REF-03Correct words, heavy classroom noise60–85Noise robustness
REF-04Wrong words, fluent delivery0–30Scoring fluency instead of accuracy
REF-05Half the sentence onlycompleteness < 60Completeness ignored
REF-06SilenceRejected before billingWasting paid API calls
REF-07A different language entirelyLow + no crashUnhandled service response
REF-0860 s at the duration limitScored, no timeoutGateway timeout on long clips
Known defect class · systematic false negatives

Lingotran's pronunciation feedback has historically penalised accented-but-correct speech, marking REF-02-type clips as errors. The learners most affected are exactly Lingotran's core users. This will never show up in a test suite that uses only native-speaker clips or stubbed responses — the stub always returns a good score. REF-02 must be in the nightly real-audio run, with a floor assertion, permanently.

7.4 Failure handling

Speech service behaviourCorrect app behaviourTest
TimeoutRetain clip, do not consume attempt, offer retryBlock the endpoint mid-flight
429 quota exceededQueue or degrade gracefully, never a raw errorExhaust the staging quota deliberately
Partial payload (no phonemes)Show overall score, hide phoneme panelStub a response with fields removed
Malformed JSON502 to the client, alert raisedStub garbage
Latency > 10 sProgress indicator, no double submitDelay the stub by 15 s
Privacy — a standing check

Learner audio is personal data, and a large share of Lingotran's learners are minors. For any change touching capture or upload, confirm: audio goes only to the contracted Azure region, retention matches the school agreement, clips are deleted when a learner is removed, and no third-party endpoint appears in the network tab. Browser-native speech APIs in particular may transmit audio to servers outside the contracted sub-processor list — verify in DevTools, not in documentation.

08 Automation · ATDD to pipeline5 p

8.1 TDD and ATDD — who owns what

Test-Driven Development is a developer practice. QA never runs the red-green-refactor loop. What QA needs is literacy: the ability to read a test-driven pull request and judge it.

Read the PR and askWhat a bad answer looks like
Do the tests assert behaviour or implementation?Assertions on mock call counts and internal state — they will pass through a refactor that breaks the feature
Were they written with the code or after?One giant test per function, named test1, added in the final commit
What is already covered at unit level?Nothing — so your E2E suite must carry the whole burden
What can unit tests structurally not reach?Speech responses, migration order, real microphones, multi-instance behaviour

ATDD is the QA-owned equivalent. Acceptance criteria are written as Given/When/Then before the sprint opens (Module 3.2), agreed with the developer, and become the Playwright spec. Same tests-first discipline, at the layer where QA has authority.

8.2 What to automate

CandidateVerdictReason
Login, session, refreshAutomateRuns on every build; deterministic; catastrophic if broken
Attempt limit enforcementAutomatePure logic, high value, easy to assert
Cross-school data isolationAutomateSQL assertion, seconds to run, contract-critical
API contract for all endpointsAutomateCheap, fast, catches accidental shape changes
Scoring qualityNightly onlyNon-deterministic and paid — band assertions against the REF corpus
Real microphone captureManualCannot be automated meaningfully; needs real devices
Visual layout polishManual + snapshotsSnapshot churn costs more than the bugs it finds
Exploratory chartersNeverAutomation cannot be surprised, and surprise is the point
One-off migration verificationNeverRuns once; a script costs more than doing it
The test to apply

Automate when frequency × consequence > cost of maintenance. Most flaky suites exist because someone automated something that runs twice a year.

8.3 Playwright patterns

e2e/attempts.spec.ts
test('learner cannot exceed the attempt limit', async ({ page, request }) => {
  // Set up state through the API, never through the UI — 10× faster, no flake
  const { token } = await seedLearner(request, { school: 'school.edu' });
  await loginWithToken(page, token);

  await page.goto('/lessons/greetings/ex/1');
  for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) await submitClip(page, 'REF-01.webm');

  // Assert on a role and accessible name, not a CSS class
  await expect(page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Record' })).toBeDisabled();
  await expect(page.getByText('No attempts remaining')).toBeVisible();

  // Then verify at the source of truth — the UI can lie
  const rows = await db.query(
    'SELECT count(*) FROM attempts WHERE user_id=$1 AND exercise_id=$2', [uid, eid]);
  expect(rows[0].count).toBe('3');   // pg returns bigint as string
});
RuleWhy
Seed via API, assert via UIUI setup is the single largest source of flake and runtime
Locate by role and accessible nameSurvives restyling, and doubles as an accessibility check
Never waitForTimeoutA fixed sleep is either flaky or slow, usually both
One assertion theme per testA failure should name the defect without a debugger
Verify at the databaseA green UI over a wrong row is the defect that reaches production
Fresh data per testShared fixtures create order dependence, which surfaces only in CI
Flake policy

A spec that fails intermittently is worse than no spec — it trains the team to re-run the pipeline. Quarantine on the second unexplained failure, fix within one sprint, delete if unfixed. Track flaky rate as a first-class metric.

8.4 Azure Pipelines

azure-pipelines.yml (test stages, abridged)
stages:
- stage: Build
  jobs:
  - job: UnitAndLint
    steps:
    - script: npm ci
    - script: npm run lint
    - script: npm run test:unit -- --coverage
    - task: PublishTestResults@2
      inputs: { testResultsFiles: '**/junit-*.xml' }
    - task: PublishCodeCoverageResults@2      # gate on CHANGED lines (1.2)

- stage: Integration
  dependsOn: Build
  jobs:
  - job: ApiTests
    services: { postgres: postgres15 }   # real DB, not a mock
    steps:
    - script: npm run migrate:up
    - script: npm run test:api
    - script: npm run migrate:down          # rollback is tested here (6.3)

- stage: E2E
  dependsOn: Integration
  jobs:
  - job: Playwright
    steps:
    - script: npx playwright test --shard=$(idx)/4
    - task: PublishPipelineArtifact@1       # traces + video on failure
StageBudgetBlocks
Lint + unit< 3 minPR merge
API + integration< 6 minPR merge
E2E (sharded ×4)< 10 minStaging deploy
Nightly speech corpus~20 minNothing — reports, alerts on band breach
Nightly k6 load~15 minNothing — trends tracked over time
Ten minutes

Keep PR feedback under ten minutes. Beyond that the author has context-switched, and the pipeline stops being feedback and starts being an obstacle to route around.

09 Performance, security, accessibility5 p

9.1 Performance

Lingotran's load is not uniform. It arrives in spikes shaped like a school timetable: thirty learners in one room start the same lesson within ninety seconds, four times a day.

ScenarioShapeBudget
Class login burst30 users / 90 s, one NAT IPp95 < 800 ms, zero 429
Simultaneous submission30 clips within 60 sp95 < 4 s end to end
Teacher opens class report1 user, 200 learners, 12 weeksp95 < 1.5 s
Timetable peak40 classes concurrentlyNo error-rate rise; autoscale engages
SoakNominal load, 4 hFlat memory; no connection-pool leak
k6/class-burst.js
export const options = {
  scenarios: { classroom: {
    executor: 'ramping-arrival-rate', startRate: 0, timeUnit: '1s',
    stages: [{ target: 30, duration: '90s' }, { target: 0, duration: '30s' }],
    preAllocatedVUs: 40,
  }},
  thresholds: {
    http_req_duration: ['p(95)<800'],
    http_req_failed:   ['rate<0.001'],
    'http_req_failed{status:429}': ['count==0'],   // the NAT trap — see 10.2
  },
};
Always load-test from a single source IP

Every learner in a school shares one NAT address. A load test that spreads across many IPs will never reproduce the failure that actually takes a school offline.

9.2 Security

AreaTestExpected
Broken object accessLearner A requests learner B's attempt by ID403/404 — the most common real-world API flaw
Cross-tenantTeacher at school X requests a class at school YDenied; SQL check in 6.2 returns zero
Privilege escalation{"role":"admin"} in a profile update bodyField stripped, not persisted
JWT tamperingalg:none; wrong-key signature; expired401 in all cases
Session lifecyclePassword change with a second device activeSecond device 401 on next request
User enumerationLogin with unknown vs known emailIdentical message and identical timing
Rate limitingCredential stuffing from one IPThrottled — but not so hard a school is locked out
Injection' OR 1=1 -- in every text fieldParameterised; treated as literal text
Stored XSSDisplay name <img src=x onerror=alert(1)>Escaped in every view, including PDF exports
Upload abuseRename an .exe to .webmRejected on content type, not extension
Blob URLsOpen a clip URL while signed outDenied; URLs are short-lived and signed
Error leakageForce a 500No stack trace, SQL, or version in the response
Minors

A large share of Lingotran learners are children. Any defect exposing learner identity, audio, or progress across account boundaries is a safeguarding incident with regulatory weight — not a normal severity-2 bug. Escalate immediately and never batch it into a sprint.

9.3 Accessibility — WCAG 2.1 AA

Public-sector and education buyers procure against accessibility conformance. For Lingotran this is a sales gate, not a nicety.

CheckHowLingotran-specific risk
Keyboard onlyUnplug the mouse; complete a full lessonRecord button is often a div with a click handler — unreachable
Focus visibleTab through every controlCustom-styled controls lose the ring
Screen readerNVDA / VoiceOver through one exerciseScore updates are silent — aria-live missing
Contrastaxe scan + manual on brand purpleCoral on white fails; use the text-safe variants
Non-audio pathComplete a lesson without hearing itA speech product must still serve deaf and hard-of-hearing learners
TimingRecording countdownsFixed limits disadvantage learners with motor or speech differences; must be adjustable
ErrorsTrigger every validation messageColour-only error states are invisible to colour-blind users
Zoom 200%Browser zoomLesson player clips or scrolls horizontally
Automation covers about a third

An axe scan in CI catches contrast, missing labels, and landmarks. It cannot tell you the tab order is illogical or the screen-reader announcement is meaningless. Budget manual passes for the lesson player every release.

10 Defects, RCA & production5 p

10.1 Bug report that gets fixed

LT-4471 · Sev-2

Title Attempt limit resets on page reload, allowing unlimited submissions
Environment Staging, build 2.14.3, Chrome 126, learner account at school.edu
Steps 1. Sign in as learner · 2. Open exercise with maxAttempts 3 · 3. Submit 3 clips · 4. Confirm Record is disabled · 5. Reload the page
Actual Record is enabled; a 4th attempt is accepted and stored
Expected Limit persists; 4th attempt rejected with 429
Evidence SELECT count(*) FROM attempts WHERE user_id='…' AND exercise_id='…' → 4
Correlation ID 8f2c1a94-…  ·  Impact Attempt limits are unenforceable; scores are not comparable across a class, so teacher reports are unreliable
Reported by Shashi Kumar

ElementWhy it changes the outcome
Impact stated in product terms"Teacher reports unreliable" gets prioritised; "counter resets" does not
Database evidenceProves the defect is real data, not a rendering artefact
Correlation IDTurns an hour of log searching into one query
Exact buildPrevents "cannot reproduce" on a different revision

10.2 Root cause analysis · LT-INC-0219

Summary. Monday 08:47, roughly 3,400 learners across eleven schools received 429 on sign-in. Duration 26 minutes. Resolved by raising the limit and restarting both instances.

WhyAnswer
1Users saw 429 — the login rate limiter rejected them.
2The limit is 10/min per IP, and every school presents one NAT address for all its learners.
3Per-IP is the middleware default; it was accepted unchanged when the limiter was added in LT-0904.
4The change was two lines and reviewed for correctness — nobody asked how it behaves against real customer network topology.
5The PR checklist covers correctness and coverage. It has no prompt about deployment topology or customer network shape.
Root cause

A process gap, not a coding error: security-relevant middleware is not evaluated against real customer traffic patterns.

HorizonActionOwner
ImmediateKey the limiter on IP + email rather than IP aloneBackend · same day
Short termMove counters to shared state so the limit stops scaling with instance countBackend · this sprint
DetectionAlert when 429 exceeds 1% of login traffic over 5 minutesShashi Kumar (QA) + SRE · this sprint
PreventionAdd "how does this behave for 30 users behind one NAT?" to the PR checklistQA · this sprint
Regressionk6 class-burst scenario from a single source IP, nightlyQA · this sprint

10.3 Escape analysis

For every defect that reaches production, the useful question is not "what broke" but "which gate should have caught it".

Escaped defectWhy it escapedGate to strengthen
Rate limiter per-IPTested on one instance, many IPsLoad test from a single IP at production instance count
Session survives password changeNeeds two concurrent sessions to observeMulti-session fixture in the E2E suite
Missing indexTest data was 200 rowsEXPLAIN gate on staging volumes for new queries
Accent penalty in scoringOnly native-speaker clips testedREF-02 in the nightly corpus with a floor assertion
Double submit → two attemptsManual clicking is too slowConcurrent-request test in the API suite
iPad recording failsTested on desktop Chrome onlyReal-device pass on the school's actual hardware
Soft-deleted learner in reportsDelete path never re-queried the listStanding SQL orphan/soft-delete checks (6.2)
Token retained after sign-outVerified by looking at the UIAssert token invalid at the API, not the screen

10.4 Production support

MinuteAction
0–5Confirm scope: one learner, one school, or all? Check error rate and 429 rate in Application Insights.
5–10Get a correlation ID from any affected request. It joins frontend, API, database, and speech in one trace.
10–20Establish what changed: last deploy, last migration, last flag flip, last config edit. Almost always one of these four.
20–30Mitigate — roll back, flip the flag off, raise the limit. Diagnosis comes after service is restored.
Next dayRCA with five whys, corrective actions with owners, and a regression test that would have caught it.
The rule

Mitigate first, diagnose second. A rolled-back deploy costs a sprint's pride. A 40-minute investigation while eleven schools cannot teach costs a renewal.

11 AI-assisted QA3 p

AI is fast at first drafts and structurally unreliable on facts. Use it where a wrong answer is cheap and visible; never where a wrong answer is silent.

TaskVerdictWhy
Draft test cases from a storyGoodYou review every line; omissions are obvious to you
Explain an unfamiliar PR diffGoodOrientation, then verify against the code
Convert a manual case to PlaywrightGoodThe test either runs or it does not
Generate SQL validation queriesCarefulRead every one before running — never against production
Summarise a log dumpCarefulGood at patterns, will invent a plausible cause
Decide severity or release readinessNeverNeeds customer and contract context the model does not have
Assert whether a score is correctNeverOnly the REF corpus can answer that

11.1 Prompt library

PR review orientation
You are reviewing a pull request for Lingotran (React + Node/Express + PostgreSQL).
Here is the diff: [paste]

1. Which layers of this stack does the change touch?
2. What behaviour could change that the diff does not make obvious?
3. What is now testable that was not before?
4. Which existing behaviour is most at risk of regression?
5. List 5 test cases, each naming the layer it belongs at.
Do not summarise the diff back to me. Only answer 1-5.
Test case generation
Story: [paste story + ACs]
Context: Lingotran serves schools. Learners are often minors. A class is ~30 learners
behind a single NAT IP on shared devices, many on iPad Safari.

Generate test cases as a table: ID | Case | Expected | Layer (unit/api/e2e/manual).
Include: happy path, boundaries, at least 3 negatives, 1 concurrency case,
1 accessibility case, 1 case specific to a whole class doing this at once.
Flag any AC that is ambiguous rather than guessing what it means.
Playwright conversion
Convert this manual test to a Playwright spec for Lingotran.
Rules: seed state via API not UI; locate by getByRole with accessible name;
no waitForTimeout; assert the database at the end; one assertion theme per test.
Manual case: [paste]
Log triage
These are Application Insights entries around incident [ID]: [paste]
Correlation ID: [id]
1. Reconstruct the request timeline across frontend, API, database, speech.
2. Identify the first anomalous event, quoting the exact line.
3. List up to 3 hypotheses, each with the specific evidence that would confirm it.
Mark clearly anything you inferred rather than read directly in the log.
Distrust list

AI will confidently invent Azure service limits, PostgreSQL syntax details, Playwright APIs that do not exist, WCAG success-criterion numbers, and library version behaviour. It will also produce test cases that look thorough while omitting the concurrency case that matters. Verify anything you would put your name on, and never paste learner data, audio, credentials, or connection strings into a prompt.

12 Templates & checklists4 p

12.1 Test plan — one page, no more

Release: 2.15 · QA owner: Shashi Kumar · Dates: …
In scope:    LT-1187 extended sessions · LT-1201 phoneme panel
Out of scope: billing, marketing site  — and why
Risk order:  1 session handling  2 scoring quality  3 class reports
Environments: staging (2 instances, 2M rows, real Speech)
Entry: all stories merged, staging deployed, migrations run + rolled back once
Exit:  E2E green · a11y scan clean · REF corpus within bands · no open Sev-1/2
Not being tested, accepted as risk: [the honest list — this is the most valuable line]

12.2 Release readiness

ItemStatusEvidence
All ACs verified Test run link
E2E suite green Pipeline run
Migrations applied and rolled back in staging Pipeline log
REF speech corpus within bands Nightly report
Cross-school isolation query returns zero SQL output
a11y scan clean + manual keyboard pass axe report + notes
Load test at production instance count, single IP k6 summary
Feature flags: default state confirmed Config diff
Rollback rehearsed Who, and how long it took
Open defects listed with severity Board query
Known risks stated in plain language This document
Wording matters

QA never signs "it is fine". QA signs "these are the risks, this is what is untested, this is what I recommend." The business owns the decision; QA owns the honesty of the information it is made on.

12.3 Production smoke — 5 minutes after every deploy

#CheckFail action
1Sign in as the canary learner accountRoll back immediately
2Open a lesson; content rendersRoll back
3Record and submit one clip; a score returnsRoll back
4Teacher dashboard loads a class reportInvestigate; flag off if possible
5Error rate flat for 30 min in App InsightsInvestigate
6429 rate below 1% of login trafficCheck limiter config
7Speech p95 latency within budgetCheck quota and region

12.4 PR review checklist for QA

AskLooking for
Which trace layers change?Test that layer and everything downstream (2.2)
Any new route?Auth middleware present on it and on every sibling verb
Any new query?EXPLAIN on staging volumes; index present
Any migration?Reversible; concurrent index; expand/contract for renames
Any in-process state?Behaviour at 2+ instances (2.4)
Any check-then-act?Concurrency test required (5.3)
Any new flag?Both states plus the transition
Any external call?Timeout, retry, and what happens on failure
Any user-visible text?Escaped; translated; readable by a screen reader
Do tests assert behaviour?Not mock call counts (8.1)
Anything touching learner audio?Region, retention, deletion, sub-processors (7.4)

12.5 Exploratory charter

Explore  the lesson player
With     an iPad on a throttled school wifi connection
To discover how recording behaves when the network degrades mid-clip
Timebox  45 minutes   Tester Shashi Kumar
Found:   [notes, screenshots, correlation IDs]
New cases to automate: […]     Bugs raised: […]

12.6 Metrics worth publishing

MetricTargetBehaviour it drives
Escaped defects / releaseFalling trendStrengthens the gate that let each one through
Flaky rate< 1%Keeps the suite trustworthy
PR pipeline duration< 10 minKeeps feedback inside the author's attention span
Coverage on changed lines≥ 80%Resists gaming, unlike global coverage
MTTRFallingRewards mitigation speed over diagnosis pride
REF corpus band breachesZeroThe only guard on scoring quality
Do not publish

Test case counts, bugs raised per tester, or automation percentage. Each one is trivially gamed and rewards volume over judgement.

12.7 Glossary

TermMeaning here
QA / QC / QEAssurance = preventing defects through process; Control = finding them by testing; Engineering = building the systems that do both.
VerificationDid we build it to spec?
ValidationDid we build a thing a teacher can actually use in a classroom?
Shift leftQA in refinement, not after merge. Module 3 is shift-left in practice.
Shift rightLearning from production — smoke, alerts, escape analysis.
Test pyramidMany fast unit tests, fewer API tests, fewest E2E. Inverted pyramids are slow and flaky.
EscapeA defect that reached production. The gate that missed it is the finding, not the defect.
FlakeA test that fails without a code change. Treated as a defect in the suite.
REF corpusThe fixed reference clips in 7.3 — Lingotran's only scoring-quality regression signal.
Expand/contractTwo-release pattern for renames so old and new code run together safely.
